1004619.etyen:
From bestemor (“grandmother”) + stykke (“act, deed; service”), with linking -s- (“interfix”). The second element is used in the sense “act or service of a particular kind”, as also in morsstykke (“favor, helping hand”). It continues Old Norse stykki (“piece”), from Proto-Germanic *stukkiją (“piece”).
Compare brorstykke (“service rendered to a brother or another close person”) and karsstykke (“feat requiring strength and skill”), parallel formations. The second element is cognate with Danish stykke, Swedish stycke, Dutch stuk and German Stück (“piece”).

1005131.etyen:
From hiss (“B-sharp”) + -iss (“semitone-raising suffix”), literally “B-sharp-sharp”. The base hiss (“B-sharp”) is formed from h (“the note B”) and -iss (“semitone-raising suffix; sharp”). The suffix -iss is from German -is (“semitone-raising suffix; sharp”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish hisis, Swedish hississ, German Hisis, Dutch bisis and Finnish hisis (“B double sharp”).
